note_claims.claim: The patient is presenting with worsening exertional breathlessness and COPD.
The patient has a history of MRC dyspnoea grade 3.
The patient has a history of morning cough with white sputum.
The patient has had two exacerbations requiring oral steroids in the last 12 months, one of which also required antibiotics.
The patient has no history of hospital admissions.
The patient has no history of ankle swelling.
The patient has no history of chest pain, haemoptysis, or weight loss.
The patient is an ex-smoker for 6 months, with an approximate smoking history of 30 pack-years.
The patient has good inhaler technique with Anoro.
The patient has received flu and pneumococcal vaccines.
The patient is prescribed Anoro Ellipta (umeclidinium/vilanterol) one inhalation once daily.
The patient is prescribed Salbutamol as needed (about twice daily).
The patient has no known drug allergies.
The patient's oxygen level is 93 percent on air.
The patient's breathing rate is 20.
The patient has bilateral wheeze.
The patient has coarse crackles at the bottom of the left lung, at the left base (new finding).
The patient's FEV1 is 52 percent of predicted, which is lower than last year.
The patient's blood eosinophil count last month was 0.35.
The patient has COPD with frequent exacerbations despite LAMA/LABA.
The patient's eosinophil count (0.35) is suitable for triple therapy (eosinophils ≥0.3).
There are new focal crackles at the left base.
The plan is to switch the patient from Anoro to Trelegy Ellipta, one puff once daily.
The patient is referred to pulmonary rehabilitation.
A chest X-ray is ordered today due to crackles at the left base.
The patient is scheduled for a clinic review in three months.
The patient should contact their GP the same day if they have increased breathlessness, sputum volume, or a change in sputum colour.
The patient should call 999 if they are very breathless.

transcript_facts.fact: Patient's oxygen level is 93 percent on air.
There is some wheeze on both sides.
There are some coarse crackles at the bottom of the left lung, at the left base.
Patient's FEV1 is 52 percent of predicted, which is a bit lower than last year.
Patient's blood eosinophil count last month was 0.35.
Patient smoked 20 cigarettes a day for 40 years.
Patient stopped smoking for ten years in the middle, resulting in a total of 30 years of smoking.
Patient is using the Anoro inhaler once a day.
Patient is using the blue inhaler maybe twice a day.
Patient might benefit from adding a steroid to their inhalers.
The clinician plans to switch the Anoro to Trelegy, one puff once a day.
The clinician plans to refer the patient to pulmonary rehabilitation.
The clinician plans to order a chest X-ray today because of the crackles at the left base.
The clinician plans to see the patient back in the clinic in three months.
Safety netting advice: Contact GP the same day if there is a flare-up, more breathlessness, more phlegm, or a change in sputum colour.
Safety netting advice: Call 999 if the patient is very breathless.
Relative states she is the one with the swollen ankles.

findings.transcript_evidence: How have things been since we last saw you? ... I'm more breathless. I have to stop halfway up the hill to the shops now. I can walk on the flat at my own pace, but I'm slower than Valerie.
findings.rationale: The note omitted the patient's MRC dyspnoea grade 3, which is a critical functional assessment for COPD severity.

findings.transcript_evidence: Relative: That's me. I'm the one with the swollen ankles.
findings.rationale: The note inaccurately summarizes the history regarding ankle swelling; the relative reported it, although the patient denied it.
